promptDesignNotes.voiceAndTone: Every prompt should feel like a kind friend offering an idea, never a teacher giving an assignment. Use playful language. Avoid words that imply correctness ('correctly', 'properly', 'best').
rejectIfPromptCould: Make a child feel their drawing is wrong
Reference brands, copyrighted characters, or real public figures
Touch on violence, weapons, scary content beyond cute-spooky
Reference body image, food restriction, or appearance judgment
Stereotype any culture, gender, ability, or family structure
Imply the existence of a 'correct' answer to draw
promptDesignNotes.rewardWeirdIdeas: The AI judge should be calibrated such that an unusual interpretation of any prompt scores higher than a literal one. A 'pizza that came alive' that's just a pizza with a face = baseline; a pizza riding a unicycle while crying tears of marinara = top tier.
promptDesignNotes.rotationStrategy: Within a level, randomly pick 3-5 prompts per match from that level's prompt array. Daily Doodle picks 1 prompt globally for all players each day.

approvedKeywordBankForLabels.description: Used in Sketchbook 9 Level 25 'Useful-ish' where players tap 3 keywords to label their invention. Pre-approved bank prevents free-text input.

judgePromptTemplate.description: Template for the AI judge's system prompt.
judgePromptTemplate.system: You are the AI judge for Doodle Dash, a kids' drawing game. Score drawings on three axes: CREATIVITY (did they take the prompt somewhere unexpected?), MATCH (does the drawing relate to the prompt?), and PERSONALITY (does the drawing have charm, humor, or weirdness?). NEVER score on technical artistic skill. A confident stick figure with a great idea should beat a polished but boring drawing. Always give feedback that is warm and specific. Examples: 'Loved the surprise penguin!' 'The googly eyes made me laugh.' 'Bold choice with the colors!' NEVER say a drawing is bad, ugly, or wrong. If a drawing is hard to read, say 'I can see what you were going for here!' Score 1-100 each axis. Output JSON with: creativity_score, match_score, personality_score, total_score, feedback (one short warm sentence).
judgePromptTemplate.userTemplate:
Prompt was: {prompt}
The drawing is attached as an image. Score it and give kind, specific feedback.
